design.question: Are opposite species-specific solar/white responses reproducible on other photographers?
design.observer_split: existing deterministic species-specific observer_folds from all 100 original attempts, one valid classified photo per observer
design.climate_units: shared pooled species SD for each fixed five-domain climate score, computed using positions only, both folds
design.model: signed solar and thermal white-fraction slopes conditional on calendar month, XYZ, other four climate domains within each fold
design.slope_units: white photo-fraction percentage points per one pooled within-species climate-domain SD
design.primary: signed solar slope Spearman crossfold correlation, on common solar/thermal support; matched thermal and direct difference form a simultaneous three-contrast family
design.sign_prediction: centered out-of-fold sign times opposite-fold signed slope, symmetrized; zero under independent directions after shared mean removal
design.inference: 5000 whole-genus bootstrap with reranking within each draw; fixed observed climate/photo frames

limitations: Repeatability concerns observed photo white fractions, not genetically verified petal morphs.
Observer folds do not separate geographic populations, individual plants, platforms, or all measurement errors.
Half-sample slopes may be noisy. A null repeatability estimate does not prove absence of species-specific biological responses.
A positive repeatability could reflect repeated environmental or spatial confounding; not direct solar causation, UV protection or selection.
Common-support species have enough residual climate variation in both folds and are not all 4475 taxa.
The signed slope estimand differs from previous unsigned pair-distance divergence; neither algebraically implies the other.
interpretation: On 433 common species, neither solar nor thermal signed response ranks are repeatable across observer folds; the paired rank-repeatability difference is unresolved. Solar signs agree in 218/433 species, with 215 opposite signs, and the centered sign-prediction score has a wide interval around zero. This does not support stable bidirectional species-specific solar slopes as the explanation of the earlier unsigned solar-distance association. Insufficient power and residual spatial/measurement structure remain possible. Thermal white-fraction slopes have a positive mean in the common set, despite no repeatable individual ranking. Slope estimates are in shared pooled species-domain SD units, not identical units/support to historical full-source coefficients. Avoid treating a mean response as a species-level prediction or fitting new thresholds to recover significance.
